cards.title: Pairing becomes a server fact: code checked at the door, PIN only to the TV
shared_surfaces: desk/src/lib/session/store.ts (Event 'join' gains code?, 'leave'; Session gains viewer?)
acceptance: case 1: GET /api/session and the first stream message for a request the proxy marked guest -> viewer 'guest', pin '' and joined false, and pages, history, memory, conversation, practice, englishLearning emptied (the lobby: screen, subject, learner name, and the draft only while the TV is on profile); the same GET marked tv -> the whole session with its pin (tools/desk-pairing-test.cjs, route handlers called in-process with a scratch DESK_DATA_DIR)

CRITIC REVISE (binding): pairing.json holds only the TV key; the pin stays only on the Session (store.ts) as today and pairing.ts reads it from getSession() when minting the desk-phone HMAC - the session is the only state (repo law), and the two copies would otherwise drift on reset.

cards.rollback: The series is test-first, then pairing.ts + proxy.ts + instrumentation.ts (new files), then the two session routes and the store's two Event members, then the clients. Reverting the series restores today's open join byte for byte; the key file it wrote under DESK_DATA_DIR is inert without proxy.ts, and leftover desk-tv/desk-phone cookies are ignored by the old routes.
cards.runner_up: The session stream stops shipping every snapped page on every clock tick: read/route.ts:23 puts the page's data URL on Session.pages, store.ts:277-278 dispatches a tick every second and store.ts:308-309 writes and pushes the whole session each time, and LandingTV.tsx:207 re-fits on every updatedAt - pages by URL, not in the session.
cards.body:
## Summary
Adopts the open backlog card 'The desk's pairing PIN is checked only in the browser; the server takes join from anyone' (.personas/memory-outbox.jsonl, L, architecture) and makes the decision it was waiting for: the TV is the browser holding the desk's key, a phone is a device that gave the code to the server, and everyone else sees a lobby. One module owns it (lib/session/pairing.ts) and one gate applies it to every API route (src/proxy.ts), so no route has to remember.

## Description
Today the PIN is a client-side courtesy: the phone compares what was typed, scanned or remembered with s.pin in three places (phone/page.tsx:65,87,95) and then posts {type:'join'}, which the server accepts from anyone (session/route.ts:11-19 has no 'join'; store.ts:196 needs no code). The server also hands the PIN to every client in GET /api/session and every stream push (route.ts:21, stream/route.ts:11-12), so the check protects nothing, and 'joined' is one session-wide flag, so a second device inherits the first one's pairing (phone/page.tsx:387). Twelve handlers reach the store and none knows who is calling.

The auth model, decided here:
- The TV key: pairing.ts mints a random key into DESK_DATA_DIR/pairing.json on first start, next to the current pin; instrumentation.ts prints 'TV: http://<ip>:<port>/tv?key=...' at every start (the Jupyter-token pattern). GET /tv?key= sets an httpOnly desk-tv cookie and redirects to /tv. An address cannot stand in for it: base-server.js:612 lets a client supply x-forwarded-for.
- A phone: POST {type:'join', code} is checked on the server against the pin; on a match the response sets desk-phone = HMAC(key, pin). A reset mints a new pin, so every phone cookie lapses and phones ask for the code again, exactly as today.
- The gate: proxy.ts (matcher /api/:path* and /tv) classifies each request from its cookies against pairing.json (mtime-cached), overwrites x-desk-role, and answers 401 to a guest everywhere except GET /api/session, GET /api/session/stream and POST /api/session. The pipeline routes are not edited at all.
- The view: pairing.view(session, role) - the TV gets the whole session; a phone gets it without the pin and with joined = true for itself; a guest gets the lobby (screen, subject, learner name, the draft while the TV is on profile). The stream computes it per connection. A guest may post only join, nav to 'pair' (the phone's 'Show the code on the TV'), and the profile name while the TV is on profile.
- In-process callers (tests, retry's internal call) carry no proxy header and keep full behaviour, so tools/desk-jobs-rules-test.cjs and tools/maths-rules-test.cjs stay green.

Contract change - every consumer:
- desk/src/tv/useSession.ts (TV and phone): post returns the Response; reconnect() reopens the stream after a join. In the write set.
- desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx: the three client compares go; join posts the code; 'That code is not on the TV.' comes from the 403; 'Forget this desk' posts {type:'leave'} to expire the cookie. In the write set.
- desk/src/app/phone/panelFor.ts and tools/phone-panel-test.cjs: unchanged, because the phone view's joined is per device (GUARD).
- desk/src/app/tv/page.tsx: a guest TV draws one On Air line, 'Not this desk's TV. Open the TV address the desk printed.' The bench's Fake phone button still joins as the TV. In the write set.
- The 9 s.pin readers (screens.tsx, LandingTV.tsx, MathsTV.tsx, EssayTV.tsx): unchanged, because the TV view keeps the pin.
- LingaPhone.tsx, useEnglish.ts, useEnglishAudio.ts, LingaTestBar.tsx and the keymap's /api/practice and /api/hint calls: same-origin fetch, so the cookie rides along. Unchanged.
- uat/driver/linga-text.cjs, uat/driver/surface.cjs: in-process store. Unchanged.
- tools/linga-ui-test.cjs: HTTP. It reads the key from its isolated DESK_DATA_DIR and opens /tv?key=. In the write set.
- Operator capture lines that open /tv (.claude/cx/config.md:36,62, .claude/contest/config.md:50, .claude/scan-sweep/config.md:33): they use the printed TV address. The builder names them in the commit for the operator; they are not code.
- desk/src/app/page.tsx: its /tv link stays key-free, because that page is LAN-public.

## Flow
- Server starts -> pairing.json holds {key, pin}; the terminal prints the TV address with the key.
- The TV opens /tv?key=... once -> desk-tv cookie -> /tv; its stream is the whole session and the Pair screen shows the pin and QR as today.
- The phone scans the QR (phoneUrl?pin=NNNN) -> the phone page posts {join, code:NNNN} -> 200 + desk-phone cookie -> reconnect() -> the phone view, joined -> follow() lands it on the confirmation.
- A stranger on the Wi-Fi opens /phone or curls /api/session -> the lobby, no pin; POST /api/hint -> 401; POST {type:'join'} -> 403.
- The TV resets -> a new pin -> the old phone cookies lapse -> the phones see the join panel.

## Expected impact
Only someone who can read the TV can pair a phone; nobody off the desk can read a learner's session, post an event or spend a model call. The PIN stops leaving the TV, and pairing is per device instead of one flag for the whole desk. The card closes the backlog item without an edit in any pipeline route. The cost is one extra step per TV browser: open the printed address once.

## Evaluation
Claim: the desk only pairs a device that gave the TV's code to the server, and only the TV receives the code
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (the 2 GUARD cases are green by design); PIN checks on the server: 0 of 3 join paths; clients that receive the PIN: every one; API handlers that check the caller: 0 of 12
After: 6 of 6, the guards still green; server-side PIN checks 3 of 3; PIN receivers: the TV only; guarded handlers 12 of 12 through one gate
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first in tools/desk-pairing-test.cjs (node:test, desk's TypeScript loader, scratch DESK_DATA_DIR, no model call)
Result: better
Gate: architecture

cards.body:
## Summary
The evening has no ending on the TV. The only way to end it is two taps on the phone. The recap it reaches counts only page hints, lists the hinted problems as prose, offers a 'Send to parent' that sends nothing, and 'Back to tonight' drops every learner, Jakub included, into Math Buddy. This card lets the TV end the evening in one press, draws what each app on the desk did tonight as one picture, and lets Select on an app reopen what that app still has on the desk.

## Description
The data is already in the session. Every maths and essay piece of work leaves a dated history line (mark.ts:101-105, read/route.ts:28-31, essay.ts:59-62), and Linga records each conversation with its time and turns (english/types.ts:50). A new pure module, tv/recapRows.ts (types only from the store, like landingRows), reads them since the start of today into one tile per app on the profile, in the desk's order:
- Math Buddy: each marked set as ticks and rings (k of n), pages read, hints and second hints as counts.
- Linga: one mark per conversation, sized by its replies.
- Essay Master: each reading as arrows, the ones to fix reversed.
An app that did nothing tonight says 'Not tonight'. The Recap screen (On Air, per DESIGN-STUDY-DESK.md:7-8) draws the tiles with thin channel tags. Only the caption slot carries a sentence, and the prose list of problem texts goes.

Keys (keys.ts):
- Menu on the landing posts session.end and fires /api/memory, which the phone's End session does today.
- On the recap the stops are the tiles, then 'Back to the desk'.
- Select on a tile opens what that app still has on the desk, through the same helpers the landing and Tonight use: continueCard's target for maths, forensicAt for this learner's reading, Linga's home.
- Back goes to the landing at rest.
'Send to parent' stops being a fake action: it becomes a non-focusable chip, 'On the parent's phone', which the phone's Recap panel (phone/page.tsx:380) makes true. The place card's caption names the new key in its one sentence: 'Select hands the desk on. Menu ends tonight.'

Gate: direction. The card adds a Menu row to the landing's D-pad, the design chosen in the contest (DESIGN-STUDY-DESK.md:63-69), and widens the recap from page hints to all three apps. Both fall inside the context's scope ('every TV screen'), and no module's design language is restyled.

## Flow
- Landing, lamp anywhere -> Menu -> the recap: three tiles (Math Buddy 4 ticks and 2 rings, Linga two conversations, Essay Master five arrows with two reversed), caption 'Good evening's work - two to look at together'.
- Right to the Math Buddy tile -> Select -> the marked sheet at its first slip, to look at together.
- Back -> Math Buddy home -> Back -> the desk, with the lamp at rest.
- Or on the recap -> Back -> the desk directly.
- Jakub: two tiles (Linga, Essay Master); Back -> the desk, never Math Buddy.

## Expected impact
The evening gets an ending on the screen where it happened, and the parent's question, 'how did tonight go?', is answered for all three apps at a glance, not for page hints alone. The recap stops being a report you read. It becomes where you choose what to look at together, one press each, and it stops sending anyone into an app that is not on their desk.

## Evaluation
Claim: the TV ends the evening in one press, the recap shows every app used tonight as a picture, and each tile opens what it names
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (the GUARD is green by design); ways to end the evening from the TV: 0; apps whose evening reaches the recap: page hints only (0 of 3 apps' own work: no sets, conversations or readings); actionable recap stops: 0 of 2 (one fake send, one exit into Math Buddy)
After: 7 of 7, the guard still green; 1 press; 3 of 3 apps; every tile acts, and the exit goes to the desk
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first in tools/tv-recap-test.cjs (node:test, desk's TypeScript loader, the real reducer on a scratch DESK_DATA_DIR, no model call), plus one Playwright journey on a worktree dev server
Result: better
Gate: direction
